article.title: Israeli forces demolish Birzeit University’s martyrs memorial
article.author: Aseel Saleh
article.content: At dawn on Monday, October 5, Israeli forces destroyed the martyrs’ memorial at Birzeit University. Basil Farraj, an assistant professor of philosophy and cultural studies at Birzeit University, told BreakThrough News that the Israeli forces came to the campus around a week ago to capture photos of the memorial, sparking suspicions that they may attempt to destroy it. Farraj suggests that the removal of the memorial came as part of Israel’s broader efforts to erase the Palestinian people’s collective memory and entrench cultural, social, and political hegemony over them, specifically at Birzeit University, due to its pioneering role in the Palestinian struggle against occupation. “The assault on the memorial constitutes a cowardly attempt that will never defeat the resilience of the Palestinian collective memory. It also reflects the failure of the Zionist project in the face of the Palestinian people’s struggle,” he emphasized. Meanwhile, the Right to Education Campaign issued a statement , condemning the offensive, and clarifying that it was carried out on the first day of the new academic year. “The destruction of a memorial to student martyrs is an assault on our collective memory, and our right to remember, preserve our history, and honour those who are part of Birzeit’s story,” the statement reads. “This attack comes within a broader pattern of scholasticide on Palestinian universities and the systematic disruption of academic life,” it continued. The campaign urged “universities, academics, students, human rights organizations, and governments worldwide to demand accountability, protect Palestinian educational institutions, and take concrete action to defend the right to education and academic freedom.” The university as a target In recent years, the Israeli forces have intensified their crackdown campaign on Palestinian universities across the occupied West Bank. There has been a particular focus on Birzeit University in northern Ramallah due to its pioneering role in the Palestinian prolonged struggle against the occupation. Not only have prominent scientists, political leaders, artists, and journalists graduate from the renowned Palestinian institution, but it has also long been called the “University of Martyrs” because dozens of its students and graduates have been killed at the hands of the Israeli military. Countless students have been arrested and the university campus has faced frequent military raids since 2002 . Read more: IOF abducts four Birzeit University female students at dawn
